greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῇ Αμαρφαλ βασιλέως Σεννααρ, Αριωχ βασιλεὺς Ελλασαρ καὶ Χοδολλογομορ βασιλεὺς Αιλαμ καὶ Θαργαλ βασιλεὺς ἐθνῶν
hint: In the reign of Amraphel, four kings of the east.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bîmê ʾAmrāpel*, *in the days of Amraphel*. The Greek has *in the reign*, βασιλεία.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *melek gôyim*, *king of Goiim*, which may be a place. The Greek translates it, *king of nations*.
The land here, where at 10:22 Αιλαμ is the son of Shem; the gloss is the one GEN 10 gave the name.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts ὁ before the name; Coislinianus, M, does not.

greek: ἐποίησαν πόλεμον μετὰ Βαλλα βασιλέως Σοδομων καὶ μετὰ Βαρσα βασιλέως Γομορρας καὶ Σεννααρ βασιλέως Αδαμα καὶ Συμοβορ βασιλέως Σεβωιμ καὶ βασιλέως Βαλακ (αὕτη ἐστὶν Σηγωρ).
hint: They make war on the five kings of the cities of the plain.

notes.text: The king of Adama is Hebrew *Šinʾāb*, but the Greek prints him with the letters of Σεννααρ, the land of 14:1. He is glossed for himself, with his own English name.
Rahlfs prints the aside in parentheses, and the reading keeps them. Σηγωρ is the Ζογορα of 13:10, Zoar, spelt another way.
ποιέω, `made`, the chain of GEN 9:24, in the plural.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone puts μετά before this last βασιλέως, as before the first two.

greek: πάντες οὗτοι συνεφώνησαν ἐπὶ τὴν φάραγγα τὴν ἁλυκήν (αὕτη ἡ θάλασσα τῶν ἁλῶν).
hint: The five gather at the salt valley, the Salt Sea.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿēmeq haśśiddîm*, *the valley of Siddim*. The Greek has *the salt ravine*, and at 14:8 and 14:10 *the salt valley*.
συμφωνέω is first *to agree in sound, be in harmony*, then *to agree with*; the Hebrew *ḥābĕrû* is *joined together*.
ἅλς is *a lump of salt*, and in the plural *salt*, which heads it here; *the sea* is ἡ ἅλς, the feminine, and is left out.

reading: [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[agreed in sound|agreed in sound, were in harmony, agreed with and held the same opinions with, made an agreement and bargained with, agreed, conspired]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the cleft|the cleft and chasm, the ravine and gully]] the [[salt|salt, brackish]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[the sea|the sea, the Mediterranean, a well of salt water]] [[of the salt|of the salt, of the lumps of salt]]).

greek: δώδεκα ἔτη ἐδούλευον τῷ Χοδολλογομορ, τῷ δὲ τρισκαιδεκάτῳ ἔτει ἀπέστησαν.
hint: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer; in the thirteenth they revolted.

notes.text: Imperfect of δουλεύω, *to be a slave*: `were being slaves`.
τρισκαιδέκατος, *thirteenth*, one sense, plain text.
ἀφίστημι, the intransitive second aorist, `stood away`, as at 12:8.

reading: twelve years [[were being slaves|were being slaves, were serving and being subject to]] to [[name:Χοδολλογομορ]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], to the thirteenth year [[stood away|stood away, stood aloof from and kept far from, lost, withdrew from, revolted from, revolted, gave up, made way and gave way, shrank from, stood aloof]].

greek: ἐν δὲ τῷ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῳ ἔτει ἦλθεν Χοδολλογομορ καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ κατέκοψαν τοὺς γίγαντας τοὺς ἐν Ασταρωθ Καρναιν καὶ ἔθνη ἰσχυρὰ ἅμα αὐτοῖς καὶ τοὺς Ομμαίους τοὺς ἐν Σαυη τῇ πόλει
hint: In the fourteenth year the four kings strike the giants, the strong nations and the Emim.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕʾet-hazzûzîm bĕhām*, *and the Zuzim in Ham*. The Greek has *strong nations together with them*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕšāwēh qiryātāyim*, *in Shaveh-kiriathaim*. The Greek names Σαυη and translates the rest, *the city*.
The Hebrew is *rĕpāʾîm*, *the Rephaim*; the Greek has γίγαντες, the word of 6:4.
One place printed as two names, each glossed.
ἅμα with a dative, the preposition: its sense *at the same time with, together with* heads it.

greek: καὶ τοὺς Χορραίους τοὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν Σηιρ ἕως τῆς τερεμίνθου τῆς Φαραν, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
hint: And the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as the terebinth of Paran.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾêl pāʾrān*, *El-paran*. The Greek reads *ʾêl* as the tree, *the terebinth of Paran*.
Rahlfs prints τερέμινθος; Middle Liddell files the tree under τέρμινθος, *the terebinth*.

(Σηιρ, from Hebrew Śēʿîr, "hairy")
(Φαραν, from Hebrew Pāʾrān, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἀναστρέψαντες ἤλθοσαν ἐπὶ τὴν πηγὴν τῆς κρίσεως (αὕτη ἐστὶν Καδης) καὶ κατέκοψαν πάντας τοὺς ἄρχοντας Αμαληκ καὶ τοὺς Αμορραίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Ασασανθαμαρ.
hint: They turn back to the spring of judgment, Kadesh, and strike Amalek and the Amorites.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿên mišpāṭ*, *En-mishpat*. The Greek translates the name, *the spring of judgment*, and the aside gives Καδης.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *kol-śĕdê hāʿămālēqî*, *all the country of the Amalekites*. The Greek has *the rulers*; *śārê*, *rulers*, differs from *śĕdê* by one letter.
πηγή's first translation is *running waters*, which Middle Liddell marks *mostly in pl.*; the singular here, as at 2:6.
ἀναστρέφω, the chain of GEN 8:11, in the participle; the lexicon's *to conduct oneself* keeps its *oneself*.

greek: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ βασιλεὺς Σοδομων καὶ βασιλεὺς Γομορρας καὶ βασιλεὺς Αδαμα καὶ βασιλεὺς Σεβωιμ καὶ βασιλεὺς Βαλακ (αὕτη ἐστὶν Σηγωρ) καὶ παρετάξαντο αὐτοῖς εἰς πόλεμον ἐν τῇ κοιλάδι τῇ ἁλυκῇ,
hint: The five kings draw up for battle in the salt valley.

notes.text: The aorist middle of παρατάσσω, so the entry's middle heads it: *to draw up one's men in battle-order*. The active's *to place side by side* is left out.
κοιλάς, *a hollow, deep valley*.

hint: Four kings against five.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out this third καί; Coislinianus, M, has it.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone adds οὗτοι after τέσσαρες.

greek: ἡ δὲ κοιλὰς ἡ ἁλυκὴ φρέατα φρέατα ἀσφάλτου· ἔφυγεν δὲ βασιλεὺς Σοδομων καὶ βασιλεὺς Γομορρας καὶ ἐνέπεσαν ἐκεῖ, οἱ δὲ καταλειφθέντες εἰς τὴν ὀρεινὴν ἔφυγον.
hint: The valley is full of bitumen pits; the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fall there, and the rest flee to the hills.

notes.text: The Hebrew doubles the word, *beʾĕrōt beʾĕrōt ḥēmār*, *pits, pits of bitumen*, and the Greek keeps the doubling.
ἐμπίπτω is first *to fall in*; the Hebrew *wayyippĕlû-šāmmâ* is *and fell there*.
The form serves the first singular and the third plural; the headword says *they*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus has φρέατα once; Coislinianus, M, has it twice.

greek: ἔλαβον δὲ τὴν ἵππον πᾶσαν τὴν Σοδομων καὶ Γομορρας καὶ πάντα τὰ βρώματα αὐτῶν καὶ ἀπῆλθον.
hint: The victors take the horse and the food of Sodom and Gomorrah.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾet-kol-rĕkuš*, *all the goods*. The Greek has ἡ ἵππος, *the horse*; *rekeš*, with the same letters, is *steeds*. So again at 14:16 and 14:21.
ἵππος is *a horse, mare*, and ἡ ἵππος, collectively, *horse, cavalry*; the entry's senses for the plural and its phrases are left out.
Both forms serve the first singular and the third plural; the headwords say *they*.

reading: [[they took|they took, they received, they took hold of and grasped and seized]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the horse|the horse and mare, the horse and cavalry]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] the [[name:Σοδομων]] and [[name:Γομορρας]] and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the things which are eaten|the things which are eaten, the foods, the meats]] of them and [[they went away|they went away, they departed from, they departed, they departed from life]].

greek: ἔλαβον δὲ καὶ τὸν Λωτ υἱὸν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ Αβραμ καὶ τὴν ἀποσκευὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπῴχοντο· ἦν γὰρ κατοικῶν ἐν Σοδομοις.
hint: They take Lot too, who lived in Sodom.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *rĕkušô*, *his goods*. ἀποσκευή, from LSJ, is first *removal, riddance*, then *baggage*.
The imperfect of ἀποίχομαι, *to be gone away*: `were being gone away`.
εἰμί with a participle, `was, and kept on being,`.

(Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")

greek: Παραγενόμενος δὲ τῶν ἀνασωθέντων τις ἀπήγγειλεν Αβραμ τῷ περάτῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ κατῴκει πρὸς τῇ δρυὶ τῇ Μαμβρη ὁ Αμορις τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ Εσχωλ καὶ ἀδελφοῦ Αυναν, οἳ ἦσαν συνωμόται τοῦ Αβραμ.
hint: A survivor tells Abram the Hebrew, who lives by the oak of Mamre.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lĕʾAbrām hāʿibrî*, *to Abram the Hebrew*. The Greek has περάτης, from περάω, *to cross*; LSJ gives its *wanderer, emigrant* as the explanation of Ἑβραῖος.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *hāʾĕmōrî*, *the Amorite*, of Mamre. The Greek transliterates it, and prints it in the nominative after the dative τῇ Μαμβρη.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *baʿălê bĕrît-ʾAbrām*, *masters of Abram's covenant*. The Greek has συνωμόται, *fellow-conspirators, confederates*.
παραγίνομαι's first sense is *to be beside, to be by or near, attend upon*, of which Perseus tags only *near, attend upon*; the headword takes *been* from the untagged words around it.
The aorist passive of ἀνασώζω, *to recover what is lost, rescue*, in the passive; the entry's *Pass. to return safe* ends the chain, and its middle senses are left out.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐν for πρός.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts τοῦ before the second ἀδελφοῦ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

(Αμορις, from Hebrew hāʾĔmōrî, "the Amorite")
(Εσχωλ, from Hebrew ʾEškōl, "cluster")
(Αυναν, from Hebrew ʿĀnēr, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ἀκούσας δὲ Αβραμ ὅτι ᾐχμαλώτευται Λωτ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, ἠρίθμησεν τοὺς ἰδίους οἰκογενεῖς αὐτοῦ, τριακοσίους δέκα καὶ ὀκτώ, καὶ κατεδίωξεν ὀπίσω αὐτῶν ἕως Δαν.
hint: Abram musters three hundred and eighteen of his household and pursues as far as Dan.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyāreq*, *and he led forth*. The Greek has *numbered*.
The perfect passive of αἰχμαλωτεύω, *to take prisoner*, one sense and plain text, with the perfect's standing state.
Three numerals, each plain text: `three hundred ten and eight`.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads the aorist, ᾐχμαλωτεύθη.

reading: [[having heard|having heard, having had hearing of, having heard tell of, having hearkened and given ear, having listened to and obeyed]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβραμ]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] has been taken prisoner and stands taken prisoner [[name:Λωτ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of him, [[numbered|numbered, counted and reckoned up, counted out and paid, reckoned and counted as, was reckoned, was counted]] the [[one's own|one's own, pertaining to oneself, private and personal, peculiar and separate and distinct, peculiar and different, strange and unaccustomed]] [[born in the house|born in the house, homebred]] of him, three hundred ten and eight, and pursued closely [[after|after, backwards, back and back again, again, hereafter, behind]] them [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[name:Δαν]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, "judge")

greek: καὶ ἐπέπεσεν ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς τὴν νύκτα, αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ παῖδες αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπάταξεν αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐδίωξεν αὐτοὺς ἕως Χωβα, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν ἀριστερᾷ Δαμασκοῦ.
hint: He falls on them by night and pursues them to Hobah, left of Damascus.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyēḥālēq ʿălêhem laylâ*, *and he divided himself against them by night*. The Greek has *fell upon them*.
The Hebrew *miśśĕmōʾl*, *on the left*, where facing east the left is the north. ἀριστερός is headed `left`, as at 13:9.
*to pursue closely*, one sense, plain text.

reading: and [[fell upon|fell upon, attacked and assailed]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] them [[the night-season|the night-season, the night, the watches of the night, the dark of night, the night of death]], he and [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids]] of him, and [[beat|beat, knocked, struck and smote, knocked at]] them and [[pursued|pursued, chased and hunted, was a follower of and attached oneself and sought after, followed and waited for, drove and chased away and banished, impelled and sped on her way, urged on, drove and drove on, galloped and sped and ran, prosecuted and brought an action against, accused of and prosecuted for, avenged]] them [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[name:Χωβα]], which is [[in left|within, inside of, and by means of left and on the left, the left hand, boding ill and ominous]] [[name:Δαμασκοῦ]].

names.gloss: (Χωβα, from Hebrew Ḥôbâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Δαμασκός, from Hebrew Dammeśeq, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἀπέστρεψεν πᾶσαν τὴν ἵππον Σοδομων, καὶ Λωτ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπέστρεψεν καὶ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ τὸν λαόν.
hint: He brings back the horse of Sodom, Lot, his goods, the women and the people.

notes.text: ἀποστρέφω, `turned`, the chain of GEN 3:19, in the aorist.
λαός is first *the people*; its later senses, *Jews* and *Christians*, keep their capitals.

reading: and [[turned|turned, turned back, turned away, turned oneself about, brought back]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the horse|the horse and mare, the horse and cavalry]] [[name:Σοδομων]], and [[name:Λωτ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of him [[turned|turned, turned back, turned away, turned oneself about, brought back]] and [[the existing circumstances|the existing circumstances, the present advantages, what belongs to one, the possessions and means]] of him and [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women]] and [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians]].

greek: Ἐξῆλθεν δὲ βασιλεὺς Σοδομων εἰς συνάντησιν αὐτῷ — μετὰ τὸ ἀναστρέψαι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τοῦ Χοδολλογομορ καὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῶν μετʼ αὐτοῦ — εἰς τὴν κοιλάδα τὴν Σαυη (τοῦτο ἦν τὸ πεδίον βασιλέως).
hint: The king of Sodom meets him in the valley of Shaveh, the king's plain.

notes.text: Rahlfs sets the clause between dashes; the reading keeps it in commas, since dashes mark the chains.
κοπή, *a cutting in pieces, slaughter*. Hebrews 7:1 has the same words of the same return: ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων.
συνάντησις, *a meeting*, one sense, plain text.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Σαυην.

reading: [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[a king|a king, a chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia]] [[name:Σοδομων]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] a meeting to him, [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[to turn upside down|to turn upside down, to upset, to turn back and bring back, to rally, to turn back and return and retire, to dwell, to conduct oneself, to revolve, to face about]] him [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the cutting in pieces|of the cutting in pieces, of the slaughter]] of [[name:Χοδολλογομορ]] and [[of the kings|of the kings, of the chiefs, of the hereditary kings, of the lords and masters and householders, of the seconds of the nine archons, of the kings of Persia]] the [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] him, [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the hollow|the hollow, the deep valley]] the [[name:Σαυη]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[the plain|the plain, the flat, the plain flat open country]] [[of a king|of a king, of a chief, of an hereditary king, of a lord and master and householder, of the second of the nine archons, of the king of Persia]]).

greek: καὶ Μελχισεδεκ βασιλεὺς Σαλημ ἐξήνεγκεν ἄρτους καὶ οἶνον· ἦν δὲ ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου.
hint: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine.

notes.lemma: Μελχισεδεκ βασιλεὺς Σαλημ … ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου
notes.text: Hebrews 7:1 quotes the titles: Μελχισέδεκ, βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; and 7:2 reads the two names, βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης and βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης.
The Hebrew is *kōhēn lĕʾēl ʿelyôn*, *priest of El Elyon*; the Greek has θεός for *ʾēl* and ὕψιστος for *ʿelyôn*.
ὕψιστος, *highest, loftiest*, the superlative filed as its own entry; the article before it is plain `the`.
οἶνος, `wine`, plain, as at 9:21.

reading: and [[name:Μελχισεδεκ]] [[a king|a king, a chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia]] [[name:Σαλημ]] [[carried out of|carried out of, carried out, carried off, carried out of the sea and threw ashore, brought forth, brought forth and produced, brought about and accomplished, brought out and published, delivered, brought forward, disclosed and told and betrayed, put forth and exerted, bore the marks of, carried to a certain point, shot forth, ran away, came to fulfilment and came to an end, came to land and was cast ashore, was carried beyond bounds and carried away]] [[cakes|cakes, loaves of wheat-bread, breads]] and wine; was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[a priest|a priest, a sacrificer, a minister]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] the [[highest|highest, loftiest]].

names.gloss: (Μελχισεδεκ, from Hebrew Malkî-ṣedeq, "king of righteousness")
(Σαλημ, from Hebrew Šālēm, usually connected with šālôm, "peace")

greek: καὶ ηὐλόγησεν τὸν Αβραμ καὶ εἶπεν Εὐλογημένος Αβραμ τῷ θεῷ τῷ ὑψίστῳ, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν,
hint: He blesses Abram by God Most High, who made heaven and earth.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *qōnēh šāmayim wāʾāreṣ*, *possessor* or *maker of heaven and earth*. The Greek has ἔκτισεν.
κτίζω is first *to people, build houses and cities, colonise*; *to create* comes later in the entry.
The words of GEN 1:1, and their chains.
The perfect passive participle of εὐλογέω, *to speak well of*, with the perfect's standing state.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed]] [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[having been spoken well of|having been spoken well of and remaining so, having been praised and standing praised, having been honoured and standing honoured, having been blessed and standing blessed]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only]] the [[highest|highest, loftiest]], who [[peopled|peopled, built houses and cities, colonised, founded and planted and built, planted, set up, established, created and brought into being and brought about, made, perpetrated, was founded]] [[the heaven|the vaulted arch, the sky-expanse, the region above and over]] and [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the soil, the territory, the terrestrial realm as the counterpart-below]],

greek: καὶ εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς ὁ ὕψιστος, ὃς παρέδωκεν τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποχειρίους σοι. καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων.
hint: Blessed be God, who gave your enemies into your hand; and he gives him a tenth of all.

notes.text: No verb: the Greek sets εὐλογητός, `blessed`, beside ὁ θεός, as at 9:26.
The Greek names neither giver nor receiver. Hebrews 7:2 reads Abraham as the giver, δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ, and 7:4, δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν.
δεκάτη is filed under δέκατος, *tenth*, whose second sense is the noun, *the tenth part, tithe*; used as a noun, it heads with that.
ἐχθρός used as a noun takes the entry's noun sense, *one's enemy*, before the adjective's *hated, hateful*.

reading: and blessed [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] the [[highest|highest, loftiest]], who [[gave|gave, handed over to another and transmitted, transmitted and imparted, delivered up and surrendered, betrayed, committed, gave up, handed down, granted and bestowed, offered and allowed]] [[the one's enemies|the one's enemies, the hated and hateful, the hostile and at enmity with]] of you [[under the hand|under the hand and in hand, under any one's hand and under command and subject, into one's power]] to you. and [[gave|gave, granted, provided, gave over and delivered up]] to him [[tenth part|tenth part, tithe, tenth day, tenth day after birth, naming-day, tenth]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ βασιλεὺς Σοδομων πρὸς Αβραμ Δός μοι τοὺς ἄνδρας, τὴν δὲ ἵππον λαβὲ σεαυτῷ.
hint: The king of Sodom: give me the men, keep the horse.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[a king|a king, a chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia]] [[name:Σοδομων]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[give|give, grant, provide, give over and deliver up]] to me [[the men|the men, the men in the prime of life]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the horse|the horse and mare, the horse and cavalry]] [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize]] for yourself.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Αβραμ πρὸς βασιλέα Σοδομων Ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τὸν ὕψιστον, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν,
hint: Abram swears by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth.

notes.lemma: Ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τὸν ὕψιστον
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *hărîmōtî yādî ʾel-YHWH ʾēl ʿelyôn*, *I have lifted my hand to YHWH, God Most High*. The Greek has the future, *I will stretch out*, and no *YHWH*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβραμ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[a king|a king, a chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia]] [[name:Σοδομων]] [[I will stretch out|I will stretch out, I will spread out, I will put forth]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm]] of me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] the [[highest|highest, loftiest]], who [[peopled|peopled, built houses and cities, colonised, founded and planted and built, planted, set up, established, created and brought into being and brought about, made, perpetrated, was founded]] [[the heaven|the vaulted arch, the sky-expanse, the region above and over]] and [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the soil, the territory, the terrestrial realm as the counterpart-below]],

greek: εἰ ἀπὸ σπαρτίου ἕως σφαιρωτῆρος ὑποδήματος λήμψομαι ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν σῶν, ἵνα μὴ εἴπῃς ὅτι Ἐγὼ ἐπλούτισα τὸν Αβραμ·
hint: He will take nothing of the king's, not a thread or a sandal strap.

notes.text: An oath with its curse left unsaid, as the Hebrew *ʾim* is: *if I take*, meaning *I will not take*. εἰ is plain `if`.
σπαρτίον, *a small cord*, one sense, plain text; σφαιρωτήρ, from LSJ, *thong, latchet*.
σός used as a noun in the neuter plural, *thy property*, with the article the Greek prints; the entry's other noun senses belong to the masculine and the singular.
Capitalised because it opens the words Abram will not let the king say, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: if [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] of a small cord [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[of thong|of thong and latchet, of a ball, of knop]] [[of a sole bound under the foot with straps|of a sole bound under the foot with straps, of a sandal, of a half-boot]] [[I will take|I will take, I will receive, I will take hold of and grasp and seize]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the thy property|of the thy property, of the thy interests, of the thy and thine and of thee]], [[that|that, in order that]] not [[you may say|you may say, you may speak, you may declare, you may call by name, you may tell]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] I [[I made wealthy|I made wealthy and enriched, I gained one's wealth]] [[name:Αβραμ]];

greek: πλὴν ὧν ἔφαγον οἱ νεανίσκοι καὶ τῆς μερίδος τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῶν συμπορευθέντων μετʼ ἐμοῦ, Εσχωλ, Αυναν, Μαμβρη, οὗτοι λήμψονται μερίδα.
hint: Only what the young men ate, and the share of Eshcol, Aner and Mamre.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew order is *ʿĀnēr ʾEškōl ûMamrēʾ*. The Greek has Eschol first.
πλήν with a genitive, the preposition, so its sense for that case heads it, *more than*; the adverb's senses follow.
συμπορεύομαι, the chain of GEN 13:5, in the aorist participle.

reading: [[more than|more than, except, save, short of, save in respect, but, than, much like, only not, except that, save that, save so far as]] of which [[they ate|they ate, they ate of]] the youths and [[of the part|of the part, of the portion, of the share, of the parcel, of the contribution, of the part and division and class]] [[of the men|of the men, of the men in the prime of life]] [[of the ones having gone|of the ones having gone, of the ones having journeyed together, of the ones having come together]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] me, [[name:Εσχωλ]], [[name:Αυναν]], [[name:Μαμβρη]], [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[they will take|they will take, they will receive, they will take hold of and grasp and seize]] [[a part|a part, a portion, a share, a parcel, a contribution, a part and division and class]].
